com.esignal.jstandard.event

Interface ConnectionListener

  • All Superinterfaces:
    java.util.EventListener
    All Known Implementing Classes:
    ConnectionAdapter

    public interface ConnectionListener
extends java.util.EventListener
    The main purpose of this client implemented listener is to process events while establishing and closing connections. As of version 1.19.0, the API will automatically attempt to re-establish connections if the reason for the disconnection allows for it. If you would like to continue to manage connections manually, you must set the property of jstandard.DBC.manualConnect to true in the jstandard.properties configuration file. Please see below for examples of the sequence of events that you will receive based on whether or not the API will automatically re-establish connections and whether or not the disconnection was client driven or server driven. Please bear in mind that all scenarios listed below assume that a connection is already established. Automatic Connection Re-establishment Enabled: Scenario 1 : User driven disconnection -onDisconnecting with a status of SUCCESS to indicate that the API has received the request to initiate disconnection. -onDisconnected with a status code to indicate if there were any errors or not during disconnection. Scenario 2 : Server driven disconnection and reason allows for automatic reconnection -onDisconnecting with a status code indicating why the connection is being disconnected. -onDisconnected with a status of SUCCESS -onConnecting one or more times until you reach the appropriate server destination. -onConnected or onError depending upon whether the server accepted the connection request or not. Scenario 3 : Server driven disconnection and reason does not allow for automatic reconnection -onDisconnecting with a status code indicating why the connection is being disconnected. -onDisconnected with a status code to indicate if there were any errors or not during disconnection. Automatic Connection Re-establishment disabled: Scenario 1 : User driven disconnection -onDisconnecting with a status of SUCCESS to indicate that the API has received the request to initiate disconnection. -onDisconnected with a status code to indicate if there were any errors or not during disconnection. Scenario 2 : Server driven disconnection -onDisconnecting with a status code indicating why the connection is being disconnected. -onDisconnected with a status code to indicate if there were any errors or not during disconnection.

      • onConnecting

      • onDisconnecting

        void onDisconnecting(ConnectionEvent connectionEvent)
        As soon as any manager begins the process of disconnecting, or is in the process of being disconnected due to other issues with the server, this method will be called. The following error codes signify a reason for disconnect that will not result in automatic reconnection. DBCAPI_ERROR.MUST_UPGRADE DBCAPI_ERROR.WRONG_USERNAMEPASSWORD DBCAPI_ERROR.NOT_ENTITLED DBCAPI_ERROR.NOT_AUTHORIZED DBCAPI_ERROR.UPGRADEVERSION DBCAPI_ERROR.ADDRESS_CHANGE DBCAPI_ERROR.NOT_ENDOFDAY
        Parameters:
        connectionEvent - ConnectionEvent value with information.

      • onDisconnected

        void onDisconnected(ConnectionEvent connectionEvent)
        As soon as any manager successfully disconnects, this method will be called.
        Parameters:
        connectionEvent - ConnectionEvent value with information

      • onError

        void onError(ConnectionEvent connectionEvent)
        As soon as any manager fails in the process of connecting or disconnecting, this method will be called. The client should be reading the ConnectionException in this case and appropriately handle it.
        Parameters:
        connectionEvent - ConnectionEvent value with information
